# Implementation Plan: Codex iteration-engine runaway-spawn guard (no-collab iteration profile)

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"ralph-codex-iteration-engine-runaway-spawn-guard"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph --from-brainstorm` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/ralph-codex-iteration-engine-runaway-spawn-guard/plan.md`.*

## Overview

A codex 0.135 iteration driving a ralph **single-story implementation** rabbit-holed spawning runaway multi-agent (v1 Collab) sub-agents — ~10 min / ~383K tokens during job `codex-ralph-member-multi-agent-adapter` story US-002 — and burned budget without converging. This plan gives ralph single-story **codex** iterations an execution profile that **disables (or caps) sub-agent spawning** at `codex exec` time, while **preserving** multi_agent_v2 for brainstorm/review/lens fan-out and for codex crew **members** (the v5.53.0 `codex-lowering.mjs` adapter) — *mode separation*. It also adopts `iterationEngine=copilot` as the documented supported default for impl iterations as an interim safety net (D-002).

The plan **opens with a mandatory GO/NO-GO spike** (US-001). The GO outcome is **well-supported but spike-gated, not assumed**: first-hand codex-rs source reading shows `Feature::Collab` (key `multi_agent`, `Stage::Stable`, `default_enabled: true`) gates `add_collaboration_tools` (`spec_plan.rs:297,639`), and codex exposes a **first-class, validated `--disable <FEATURE>` CLI flag documented as equivalent to `-c features.<name>=false`** (`cli/src/main.rs:786-795`). So `codex exec --disable multi_agent` (≡ `-c features.multi_agent=false`) is the expected disable surface. What the spike still must prove empirically is that forcing a `Stable` default-on feature to `false` actually suppresses the v1 spawn-tool *exposure* on 0.135 and that replaying US-002 no longer rabbit-holes.

This is a **single-repo submodule task** scoped to `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph`. A codex-submodule fork patch is the **last-resort rung only if the spike rejects the config disable**, and — per the codexu dual-repo rule (`/implement-with-ralph` targets one repo/PRD per job) — it is **NOT a chained story in this impl job**: on a config NO-GO the plan STOPS at the US-001 verdict and a separate codex-targeted plan/job is spawned. The plan describes that codex-patch worktree/two-commit shape for handoff continuity; this job does not implement it.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/ralph-codex-iteration-engine-runaway-spawn-guard/selected-direction.md` (D-001, @ 6c0af6fa). Full research at `.ralph/jobs/ralph-codex-iteration-engine-runaway-spawn-guard/research-brief.md`.

- **Iteration path:** `plugins/ralph/src/ralph.mjs:112` `resolveEngine(...)` → `:917` `runEngineIteration(...)` (builds `--prompt prompts/<engine>.md --output … --effort … --text <hdr> --section "## prd.json" <prd>`; passes **no** collab flag, **no** `--timeout-ms`) → `:978` `resolveEngineScript` → `src/<engine>-exec.mjs`.
- **codex-exec argv:** `plugins/ralph/src/codex-exec.mjs:120-131` — `exec - --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=<effort> --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -o <out>`. **Already passes a `-c key=value`** — adding `-c features.X=…` (or `--disable <feature>`) is trivial. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1200000` (`:76`, a *generous 20-min* backstop — NOT a 4-min reap). This actually **strengthens the thesis**: the ~10-min US-002 runaway ran under an already-20-min timeout, so it was never timeout-reaped — confirming a **spawn guard, not a timeout change**, is the fix. (Any further timeout tuning remains OUT of scope, owned by `ralph-codex-exec-default-timeout-too-short`.)
- **codex-rs (submodule `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`, v `0.135.0-copilot-api.1`):**
  - `features/src/lib.rs:939-944` `Feature::Collab` key `"multi_agent"` `Stage::Stable` **default_enabled: true** (v1 Collab, the runaway culprit, default ON).
  - `features/src/lib.rs:946-950` `Feature::MultiAgentV2` key `"multi_agent_v2"` default_enabled: false (already off in the iteration).
  - `features/src/lib.rs:951-956` `Feature::SpawnCsv` key `"enable_fanout"` default false; `:512-513` `if SpawnCsv && !Collab { enable(Collab) }` (won't re-enable a disabled Collab unless fanout on).
  - `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:297` `collab_tools_enabled = multi_agent_v2_enabled || Collab.enabled`; `:639-726` `add_collaboration_tools` injects spawn tools only when enabled (v2 branch 642-694; v1 branch 695-725). **Both off ⇒ zero spawn tools.** ⇒ disabling Collab is the clean lever.
  - **CAP CORRECTION (copilot review, verified):** `max_concurrent_threads_per_session(turn_context)` at `spec_plan.rs:353-359` is `multi_agent_v2_enabled(turn_context).then_some(config.multi_agent_v2.max_concurrent_threads_per_session)` — it returns `Some(N)` **ONLY when multi_agent_v2 is enabled**, else `None`. The v1 SpawnAgentHandler receives it at `:714` but gets `None` for v1-Collab-only. ⇒ **`-c features.multi_agent_v2.max_concurrent_threads_per_session=1` does NOT cap v1 Collab.** Capping is only possible by *enabling v2 capped to 1* — a different tool surface (v2 tools, not v1), not a v1 cap. So the escalation ladder is: **disable (clean) → fork patch**; the "cap" is a less-preferred v2-substitution variant, not a v1 cap.

Prior-art: `spike-verdict.json:7` confirms `--enable multi_agent_v2` ≡ `-c features.multi_agent_v2=true` works on 0.135.

### Technical Constraints
- **codex sub-agent spawns are internal codex threads/agents, NOT OS child processes** (architect agent). A ralph-side `codex.exe` child-process-count guard is therefore **not a reliable collab-spawn detector** — **D-003 in its child-count form is non-viable** (matches the brainstorm's disconfirming observation). The fallback if the config knob fails is a codex fork patch (rung 3), not D-003.
- Operator hard rule: **NO wall-clock circuit-breaker on iterations.** Any lens timeout uses `--timeout-ms >= 1200000` (20 min); never short.
- **codex version-fragility:** the knob/config surface is pinned to 0.135; re-verify on the next codex rebase (≥0.137).
- **Submodule discipline (codexu AGENTS.md + plugins/ralph AGENTS.md):** ralph ships need **6 version stamps** in sync + AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG; regenerate `.copilot-plugin/` AND `.codex-plugin/` artifacts; pass the Copilot + Codex release gates. Two-commit flow (submodule commit → codexu pointer bump). codexu root `CLAUDE.md` is gitignored — never `git add` it.

## Approach

### Architecture
Per-profile tool exposure. Add an opt-in flag to `codex-exec.mjs` that, when set, appends the spike-confirmed disable surface (`--disable multi_agent` and/or `-c features.multi_agent=false`, belt: `--disable enable_fanout`) so codex collaboration spawn tools are not exposed. `runEngineIteration` passes the flag **only for the codex single-story iteration**. Every other `codex-exec.mjs` caller (lens fan-out, members via the lowered recipe — a separate path entirely) is unaffected. The config-level disable is the load-bearing layer; `prompts/codex.md` anti-spawn guidance is advisory defense-in-depth.

### Implementation Strategy
1. **Spike first (US-001)** — confirm the disable surface + replay US-002. Escalation ladder, **disable-or-patch only** (the v1 cap is not available — see CAP CORRECTION): (a) **first-class disable** `codex exec --disable multi_agent` (≡ `-c features.multi_agent=false`; belt `--disable enable_fanout`); (b) **fork patch** (separate codex plan — see below) only if (a) cannot suppress the v1 spawn tools. (A v2-substitution variant — enable multi_agent_v2 capped to 1 thread — is NOT a v1 cap and changes the tool surface; recorded as a non-preferred alternative, not a rung.) The spike's recorded verdict selects the surface the rest of the plan wires, OR triggers the NO-GO stop.
2. **codex-exec.mjs flag (US-002)** — implement the confirmed disable surface behind a default-off flag.
3. **ralph.mjs wiring (US-003)** — pass the flag for codex iterations only; mode-separation test.
4. **prompts/codex.md guidance (US-004)** — advisory anti-spawn rules; preserve durable-memory marker parity.
5. **D-002 (US-005)** — adopt copilot as the documented impl iterationEngine via **policy/docs** (concrete deliverables in ACs); record codex re-graduation criteria.
6. **Ship (US-006)** — version bump (6 stamps), AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG, regenerate copilot+codex artifacts, release gates, tests.
7. **NO-GO branch (NOT a story in this job):** if US-001 finds the config disable cannot suppress the v1 spawn tools, the impl **STOPS at the US-001 verdict**. The codex fork patch is a SEPARATE codex-targeted plan/job (per the codexu dual-repo rule: `/implement-with-ralph` targets one repo/PRD per job; a codex-submodule patch cannot be expressed as a story in this toolkit-plugin PRD). The lead spawns that separate plan with the spike verdict as its seed.

## Scope

### In Scope
- US-001 GO/NO-GO spike (mandatory, opens the plan): confirm the codex collab **disable** surface on 0.135 (`--disable multi_agent` / `-c features.multi_agent=false`) suppresses v1 spawn-tool exposure + replay US-002 with it.
- A codex single-story **iteration profile** that disables sub-agent spawning, threaded only through `runEngineIteration` → `codex-exec.mjs`.
- Anti-spawn guidance in `prompts/codex.md` (advisory).
- D-002 adopted (policy/docs-only): copilot as the documented supported impl `iterationEngine`; schema default unchanged.
- Verified mode separation (multi_agent_v2 preserved for lenses + codex members; v5.53.0 `codex-lowering.mjs` not regressed).
- Ralph plugin ship (6 stamps, docs, regenerated artifacts, gates, tests).

### Out of Scope
- **The codex fork patch** (gating `add_collaboration_tools` in codex-rs) — only triggered on a config-disable NO-GO, and then as a SEPARATE codex-targeted plan/job (dual-repo rule), NOT a story in this toolkit-plugin job.
- **codex-exec lens timeout / `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`** — already a generous 20-min default (`:76`); any further tuning owned by `ralph-codex-exec-default-timeout-too-short`.
- **Any wall-clock circuit-breaker on iterations** (operator hard rule).
- **D-003 ralph-side child-process-count guard** — research shows codex spawns are internal threads, not OS children, so a child-count signal is non-viable; not implemented. (Documented in Risk Areas.)
- A schema-default flip codex→copilot (D-002 is policy/docs-only; see Open Question 4).
- Changing codex MEMBER fan-out behavior or the v5.53.0 lowering adapter.

## Risk Areas
- **Spike disable rejection:** a `Stable` default-on feature might resist being forced `false`. Mitigation: the `--disable <feature>` flag is first-class and validated (`cli/src/main.rs:786-795`), so it should fail loud rather than silently no-op; if it genuinely cannot suppress the v1 tools, the plan STOPS at US-001 NO-GO and a separate codex fork-patch plan is spawned (dual-repo rule). No v1 cap exists as a middle rung (see below).
- **No v1 cap (verified):** `max_concurrent_threads_per_session` only applies when multi_agent_v2 is enabled (`spec_plan.rs:354`), so it cannot cap v1 Collab. The escalation ladder is disable→fork-patch; a v2-capped-to-1 substitution is a different tool surface, not a v1 cap.
- **Mode-separation regression:** an over-broad change in `codex-exec.mjs` (unconditional disable) would also suppress collab for lens/member calls. Mitigation: flag is default-off; only `runEngineIteration` codex-path passes it; regression test pins the split.
- **D-003 non-viability** (codex spawns invisible at OS layer): accepted; the fork patch is the real fallback, not a child-count guard.
- **Version-fragility:** the feature key/flag may move on the next codex rebase (≥0.137); re-verify (tracked as a re-graduation/version note in AGENTS.md).
- **Fork-patch cost (separate plan):** rebase-gated, multi-level submodule nesting, `cargo check --workspace`. Only on a config-disable NO-GO, and owned by a separate codex plan.
- **Ship hygiene:** 6 stamps must stay in sync; codex+copilot release gates must pass; never `git add` codexu CLAUDE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Spike (US-001) — mechanically verifiable
- A `spike-verdict.json` is written stating GO/NO-GO, the confirmed disable surface (`--disable multi_agent` and/or `-c features.multi_agent=false`), and the codex version probed.
- **Tool-suppression evidence (the load-bearing GO check):** a deterministic probe shows that, with the flag, codex does NOT advertise/inject the v1 Collab spawn tools. Acceptable artifacts (record at least one): (a) a `codex exec --disable multi_agent` run whose transcript/tool list contains zero `spawn_agent`/`send_input`/`wait_agent`/`close_agent` tool advertisements; OR (b) a `RUST_LOG` (codex_core debug) sidecar showing `add_collaboration_tools` injected no spawn handlers; OR (c) a comparison run WITHOUT the flag that DOES advertise them (A/B). Baseline-vs-flag diff is the proof, not a subjective "felt fine".
- **Replay evidence (smoke, non-blocking):** replaying job `codex-ralph-member-multi-agent-adapter` US-002 under `iterationEngine=codex` + the flag does NOT reproduce the runaway (no codex child-fanout in the snapshot; iteration converges within a normal budget). Recorded as smoke evidence; flaky model behavior does NOT fail the story on its own.
- NO-GO path: if no flag/`-c` surface suppresses the v1 spawn tools, the verdict records NO-GO + reason and the plan STOPS (separate codex fork-patch plan follows).

### Implementation (US-002/US-003) — deterministic blocking tests
- The new `codex-exec.mjs` flag is **default-off**; with the flag set, the assembled codex argv contains the confirmed disable surface (unit test asserts the exact argv).
- `runEngineIteration` passes the flag **only for `engine === "codex"`**; a regression test pins the split: codex iteration → flag present; copilot iteration → absent; direct lens/member `codex-exec.mjs` callers → absent (mode separation). This is the BLOCKING criterion (not the flaky replay).
- A lens/member codex invocation path still exposes multi_agent_v2 (the v5.53.0 `codex-lowering.mjs` generator output is unchanged — assert the generated `.codex-plugin/` fan-out recipe is byte-identical pre/post).

### prompts/codex.md (US-004)
- `prompts/codex.md` carries explicit anti-spawn guidance (do NOT spawn sub-agents during a single-story iteration); the durable-memory marker block (`<!-- DURABLE-MEMORY-V1 -->`) parity check codex.md ↔ copilot.md stays green (`tests/test-durable-memory-smoke.sh`).

### D-002 (US-005) — concrete, split ACs
- **Policy/docs (the chosen target):** `plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` state, in prose, that **copilot is the recommended/supported impl `iterationEngine`** while codex iterations are gated by the no-collab profile, and document the **codex re-graduation criteria** (specific, e.g. N consecutive clean single-story codex iterations with zero spawn-tool advertisement). The create-prd / convert-to-ralph-prd skill prose notes copilot as the recommended impl engine.
- **Schema behavior (explicit non-change):** `prd-schema.json` `iterationEngine` default REMAINS `"codex"` (now safe behind the profile). No schema/converter default flip. (This resolves the Overview-vs-OpenQuestion ambiguity: "documented supported default" = docs/policy text + re-graduation criteria, NOT a schema-default change.)

### Ship (US-006)
- **No wall-clock circuit-breaker** added to the iteration path.
- 6 version stamps in sync; AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG updated; `.copilot-plugin/` + `.codex-plugin/` regenerated; `node plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --check`, `check-copilot-parity.mjs`, `--target=codex --check`, `test-codex-generator.mjs`, `validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs`, and `node plugins/ralph/tests/run.mjs` all green.
- Codexu parent: active-plugin-versions table bumped in the same commit as the submodule pointer.

## Suggested Decomposition

All stories touch the **same plugin** (`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph`) and the **same shared ship surfaces** (6 version-stamp files, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, regenerated `.copilot-plugin/`/`.codex-plugin/`). Per the parallel-spawn disjoint-surface rule, **same-plugin parallel = conflict**, so this is a single serial cluster (one impl member). US-001 is a hard gate; a config-disable NO-GO ends the job (the fork patch is a separate plan, not in this cluster).

### Cluster: codex-iteration-no-collab-profile
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`plugins/ralph/{AGENTS.md,CHANGELOG.md,.claude-plugin/plugin.json,.github/plugin/plugin.json,.codex-plugin/plugin.json}`, the 3 marketplace indexes, regenerated `.copilot-plugin/`/`.codex-plugin/`; exclusive=none across stories; risk=high (version-stamp + AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG + generated-artifact churn collide if parallelized)
- `execution_mode` rationale: Must be serialized — every story converges on the same plugin's version stamps, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG, and mechanically-regenerated artifact trees; running stories in parallel produces conflicting writes to those shared files. A single impl member runs US-001 (gate) → US-002..US-006 in order. A config-disable NO-GO ends this job; the codex fork patch is a separate single-repo plan.

## Open Questions
1. Exact disable surface on 0.135 — **[RESOLVED to spike-confirm]** `codex exec --disable multi_agent` is a first-class validated flag documented as `≡ -c features.multi_agent=false` (`cli/src/main.rs:786-795`); `Feature::Collab` key is `multi_agent` (`features/src/lib.rs:941`). The spike confirms it actually suppresses the v1 spawn-tool *exposure* (forcing a `Stable` default-on feature false).
2. Does forcing a `Stable` default-on feature to `false` via `--disable`/`-c` suppress tool exposure, or is it ignored? **[INFERRED]** the first-class `--disable` flag implies it is honored; the spike's A/B tool-advertisement probe is the proof. If ignored → NO-GO → separate fork-patch plan.
3. ~~Cap on the v1 path~~ — **RESOLVED (no v1 cap):** `max_concurrent_threads_per_session` only returns `Some` when multi_agent_v2 is enabled (`spec_plan.rs:354`), so it cannot cap v1 Collab. The ladder is disable→fork-patch; no cap rung.
4. **D-002 flip vs policy-only — DECIDED: policy/docs-only.** D-001 lands the same ship and makes codex iterations safe, so flipping the schema default codex→copilot is not required and would (per the brainstorm's own D-002 risk note) create a split-brain engine story and regress the codex-as-default-member readiness chain. Decision: document copilot as the supported impl default + codex re-graduation criteria; schema default stays `codex`. (Operator may override to the harder flip for maximum conservatism — that would be a one-line follow-up.)
5. Codex re-graduation criteria: **[INFERRED]** N consecutive clean single-story codex iterations with zero spawn-tool advertisement + the iteration profile active; record the concrete N in AGENTS.md during US-005.
6. Version-fragility on the next codex rebase (≥0.137) — re-verify the feature key/flag; note in AGENTS.md.
